I read Brett’s book and discussed it with him on my podcast. BRINK is neither pro-BiBi nor anti-BiBi (although in various sections, Brett’s quite critical of BiBi). 

But it is odd that Phil, who wasn’t in the negotiations, would so *authoritatively* dismiss the account of a colleague who was actually IN all the negotiations. 

Whether one relies on Brett’s book or just the public press accounts from that time, it’s clear that Phil simply has some of the basic facts wrong. 

He says here that Israel dropped a demand to maintain positions on the border with Egypt to get the January 2025 deal.  

Not true. Israel maintained its positions there in the Janaury ‘25 deal -- the entire corridor. 

Here's public reporting that Israel in fact stayed in the corridor in the January ‘25 deal: https://t.co/tF4OH7jHvT

This public reporting is easy to find. 

Hamas had a better offer on the table in the summer of 2024 and they never answered.

I strongly recommend reading Brett’s book from cover to cover, rather than just looking at each page through the lens of what it means for this or that political figure in Israel or the U.S.
